Name: Requiring the commissioner of consumer and worker protection to promulgate rules regarding rest areas for food delivery workers.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to requiring the commissioner of consumer and worker protection to promulgate rules regarding rest areas for food delivery workers
BodyName: Committee on Consumer and Worker Protection

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Consumer and Worker Protection

Summary: This bill would require the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) to promulgate rules requiring third-party food delivery services to provide rest areas for food delivery workers. The rest areas would include access to bathrooms, places to rest, e-bike charging stations, and storage for bikes. A third-party food delivery service would be required to provide every food delivery worker access to all rest areas, regardless of which third-party food delivery service has retained such delivery worker.  In promulgating the rules, DCWP would be required to address the number of rest areas that a third-party food delivery service must provide and the geographic areas where rest areas may be located.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to requiring the commissioner of consumer and worker protection to promulgate rules regarding rest areas for food delivery workers

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Subchapter 2 of chapter 15 of title 20 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 20-1528 to read as follows:
§ 20-1528 Provision of rest areas. a. Definitions. For purposes of this section, the following terms have the following meanings:
Bicycle with electric assist. The term “bicycle with electric assist” has the same meaning as set forth in section 102-c of the vehicle and traffic law.
Rest area. The term “rest area” means an indoor space that provides access to bathrooms, places to rest, charging stations for bicycles with electric assist, and bicycle storage.
b. No later than 1 year after the effective date of the local law that added this section, the commissioner shall promulgate rules requiring each third-party food delivery service to provide rest areas for food delivery workers. Such rules shall require a third-party food delivery service to provide all food delivery workers retained by all third-party food delivery services unrestricted access to and use of all rest areas. Such rules shall also, at a minimum, address the following:
1. The number and capacity of rest areas that each third-party food delivery service must provide, which may vary based on the number of food delivery workers retained by a third-party food delivery service; and
2. The geographic areas where a third-party food delivery service may locate rest areas, which may vary based on the areas of the city where the food delivery workers retained by a third-party food delivery service make the most deliveries.
§ 2. This local law takes effect immediately.
